segments.text: Lesson 45
segments.translation: 第45课

segments.text: Of men and galaxies
segments.translation: 论人与星系

segments.text: Listen to the tape then answer this question.
segments.translation: 听录音，然后回答问题。

segments.text: What is the most influential factor in any human society?
segments.translation: 在任何人类社会中，最有影响力的因素是什么？

segments.text: In man's early days, competition with other creatures must have been critical.
segments.translation: 在人类早期，与其他生物的竞争必定是关键的。

segments.text: But this phase of our development is now finished.
segments.translation: 但我们发展的这个阶段现在已经结束了。

segments.text: Indeed, we lack practice and experience nowadays in dealing with primitive conditions.
segments.translation: 确实，如今我们在应对原始条件方面缺乏实践和经验。

segments.text: I am sure that, without modern weapons,
segments.translation: 我确信，没有现代武器，

segments.text: I would make a very poor show of disputing the ownership of a cave with a bear, and in this I do not think that I stand alone.
segments.translation: 我在与熊争夺洞穴所有权方面会表现得很糟糕，而且我不认为只有我一个人这样想。

segments.text: The last creature to compete with man was the mosquito.
segments.translation: 最后一个与人类竞争的生物是蚊子。

segments.text: But even the mosquito has been subdued by attention to drainage and by chemical sprays.
segments.translation: 但即使是蚊子也已被排水和化学喷雾所制服。

segments.text: Competition between ourselves, person against person,
segments.translation: 我们自己之间的竞争，人与人之间，

segments.text: community against community, still persists, however; and it is as fierce as it ever was.
segments.translation: 社区与社区之间，仍然存在；而且它和以往一样激烈。

segments.text: But the competition of man against man is not the simple process envisioned in biology.
segments.translation: 但人与人之间的竞争不是生物学中设想的简单过程。

segments.text: It is not a simple competition for a fixed amount of food determined by the physical environment,
segments.translation: 这不是为由物理环境决定的固定食物量而进行的简单竞争，

segments.text: because the environment that determines our evolution is no longer essentially physical.
segments.translation: 因为决定我们进化的环境本质上不再是物质的。

segments.text: Our environment is chiefly conditoned by the things we believe.
segments.translation: 我们的环境主要由我们所相信的事物所制约。

segments.text: Morocco and California are bits of the Earth in very similar latitudes,
segments.translation: 摩洛哥和加利福尼亚是地球上纬度非常相似的地方，

segments.text: both on the west coasts of continents with similar climates, and probably with rather similar natural resources.
segments.translation: 都在大陆的西海岸，气候相似，自然资源也可能相当相似。

segments.text: Yet their present development is wholly different,
segments.translation: 然而它们目前的发展完全不同，

segments.text: not so much because of different people even,
segments.translation: 与其说是因为不同的人，

segments.text: but because of the different thoughts that exist in the minds of their inhabitants.
segments.translation: 不如说是因为其居民头脑中存在的不同思想。

segments.text: This is the point I wish to emphasize.
segments.translation: 这就是我想强调的一点。

segments.text: The most important factor in our environment is the state of our own minds.
segments.translation: 我们环境中最重要的因素是我们自己心智的状态。

segments.text: It is well known that where the white man has invaded a primitive culture,
segments.translation: 众所周知，当白人入侵原始文化时，

segments.text: the most destructive effects have come not from physical weapons but from ideas.
segments.translation: 最具破坏性的影响不是来自物质武器，而是来自思想。

segments.text: Ideas are dangerous.
segments.translation: 思想是危险的。

segments.text: The Holy Office knew this full well when it caused heretics to be burned in days gone by.
segments.translation: 圣宗教裁判所在过去的日子里深知这一点，它让异教徒被烧死。

segments.text: Indeed, the concept of free speech only exists in our modern society because when you are inside a community,
segments.translation: 确实，言论自由的概念只存在于我们现代社会，因为当你身处一个社区时，

segments.text: you are conditioned by the conventions of the community to such a degree that it is very difficult to conceive of anything really destructive.
segments.translation: 你就被社区的惯例所制约，以至于很难设想出真正具有破坏性的东西。

segments.text: It is only someone looking on from outside that can inject the dangerous thoughts.
segments.translation: 只有从外部旁观的人才能注入危险的思想。

segments.text: I do not doubt that it would be possible to inject ideas into the modern world that would utterly destroy us.
segments.translation: 我不怀疑有可能向现代世界注入足以彻底摧毁我们的思想。

segments.text: I would like to give you an example, but fortunately I cannot do so.
segments.translation: 我想给你们举个例子，但幸运的是我不能这样做。

segments.text: Perhaps it will suffice to mention the nuclear bomb.
segments.translation: 也许提到核弹就够了。

segments.text: Imagine the effect on a reasonably advanced technological society,
segments.translation: 想象一下对一个技术相当先进的社会的影响，

segments.text: one that still does not possess the bomb, of making it aware of the possibility, of supplying suffcient details to enable the thing to be constructed.
segments.translation: 一个还没有拥有核弹的社会，让它意识到这种可能性，提供足够的细节使这种东西能够被制造。

segments.text: 20 or 30 pages of information handed to any of the major world powers around the year 1925,
segments.translation: 1925年前后交给任何一个世界大国二三十页信息，

segments.text: would have been sufficient to change the course of world history.
segments.translation: 就足以改变世界历史的进程。

segments.text: It is a strange thought, but I believe a correct one,
segments.translation: 这是一个奇怪的想法，但我相信是正确的，

segments.text: that twenty or thirty pages of ideas and information would be capable of turning the present-day world upside down, or even destroying it.
segments.translation: 二三十页的思想和信息就足以颠覆当今世界，甚至摧毁它。

segments.text: I have often tried to conceive of what those pages might contain,
segments.translation: 我经常试图设想那些页面可能包含什么内容，

segments.text: but of course I cannot do so because I am a prisoner of the present-day world, just as all of you are.
segments.translation: 但我当然不能这样做，因为我是当今世界的囚徒，就像你们所有人一样。

segments.text: We cannot think outside the particular patterns that our brains are conditioned to, or,
segments.translation: 我们无法在我们大脑被制约的特定模式之外思考，或者，

segments.text: to be more accurate we can think only a very little way outside and then only if we are very original.
segments.translation: 更准确地说，我们只能在极小的范围内思考，而且只有当我们非常有独创性时才行。
